title: The B1'' swallow-yield fix misses the SLA focus rows — same visible-but-dead class at every legal window below 1272 (min 1152: a 120px dead strip per row)
evidence: app/main.odin:1203: `if app.overlay_on && app.stats_valid && rnd.noc_panel_hit(rnd.noc_panel_rect(app.view.win_w, app.view.win_h), pos) && !tray_chip_hit(app, pos) {` … app/main.odin:1221 (after the swallow): `if sla_focus_click(app, pos) {` … app/main.odin:1978: `return {8, f32(sla_row_y(v, line) - rnd.hud(v, 2)), 740, f32(rnd.hud(v, 18))}` … app/main.odin:33: `MIN_WIN_W :: 1152` … app/render/noc_overlay.odin:336: `NOC_RAIL_W        :: NOC_PANEL_W + NOC_PLATE_PAD + NOC_PANEL_MARGIN // 524 — the playfield shrink` … app/main.odin:1551 (inside draw_hud, which draws after the rail): `draw_sla_gauges(app)`
detail: The SLA rows draw after the rail (draw_hud:1551) but their fixed 740px hit rects (x 8..748) cross the plate (x >= win_w-524) at every legal window under 1272; the swallow eats those presses — the exact B1'' class.
recommended_fix: Yield to the SLA row rects in the swallow (mirror tray_chip_hit), or clamp the swallow above the bottom band; pin a press at (700, win_h-80) with the rail on at 1152x648.

title: The claimed alignment-sensitive header pin (W3'' fix) reads noc_class_columns geometry only — a revert to left-aligned headers (the r2 B1' defect) stays green
evidence: noc_overlay_test.odin:366-367: `gap := f32(sla_x - loss_r)` / `testing.expect(t, gap < hdr4, "the loss->SLA gap is narrower than the loss header - ONLY right-alignment fits (left-aligned headers collide)")` — no assert touches the draw; the untested draw site noc_overlay.odin:703-705: `noc_col(v, "del", NOC_SIZE_LABEL, NOC_LABEL, del_r, y)` / `noc_col(v, "drop", NOC_SIZE_LABEL, NOC_LABEL, drop_r, y)` / `noc_col(v, "loss", NOC_SIZE_LABEL, NOC_LABEL, loss_r, y)`
detail: The asserts pin the anchors' geometry, not the draw's alignment. Reverting the header row to left-aligned draw_mono_c at the anchors — the exact r2 B1' regression — keeps every test green.
recommended_fix: Share noc_col's draw-x computation (x_right minus measured width) with the test and assert the 'loss' header draw x — a left-alignment revert then fails.

title: The claimed rail-on zoom/pan/pullback pins (N1''/W4'' fix) are vacuous — all three legs pass under a full play_w->win_w revert
evidence: app/pullback_test.odin:282: `testing.expect(t, app.cam_zoom_to != before, "rail on: the wheel still zooms (the anchor math reads play_w)")` … :292: `testing.expect(t, app.cam_wx_to != bx || app.cam_wy_to != by, "rail on: the pan moves the camera (the clamp reads play_w)")` … :303: `testing.expect(t, app.pullback, "rail on: a distant seed still triggers the pullback (the target math reads play_w)")` … the threaded sites: app/main.odin:1891: `cx, cy := rnd.camera_anchor_center(wx, wy, pos.x, pos.y, f32(v.play_w), f32(v.win_h), fit, z_to)`
detail: All three asserts also hold with win_w threaded (recomputed: the zoom step is width-independent; the pan stays inside both clamp ranges; the terminal is off-screen at both widths) — the main.odin:1830/1891-1892/1919 call sites remain revert-green.
recommended_fix: Assert play_w-dependent outcomes at rail-on: post-zoom world right edge <= play_w; the pan clamp differs from a win_w twin at the boundary; the pullback target fits the playfield.

title: The claimed N2' fold leaves the visible-row expression duplicated verbatim — the pin can drift silently against the draw
evidence: app/render/noc_overlay.odin:629: `visible := i32((v.win_h - NOC_CONTENT_Y - NOC_CONTENT_BOTTOM) / NOC_ROW_H)` … app/render/noc_overlay_test.odin:259-260: `visible := i32((v.win_h - NOC_CONTENT_Y - NOC_CONTENT_BOTTOM) / NOC_ROW_H)` / `testing.expect(t, visible == 23, "23 visible rows at 1280x720 (574px / 24px rows)")`
detail: r2-N2' named the visible-row expression and the 84/196 literals; only the literals folded (noc_class_columns). The test pins its own copy — a draw-side formula change drifts silently green.
recommended_fix: Extract noc_visible_rows(v) used by draw_noc_panel and the test (the noc_class_columns pattern).
